summary: Snapshot is from 'cutie', a Jetson Orin Nano Super (JetPack 36.5.2, ROS 2 Humble) robot with a live ROS graph reporting 7 topics and 12 services under two apparent node namespaces (cutie_llm, cutie_speaker) but zero enumerated nodes, plus a set of USB-attached peripherals (STM32 STLink/mbed board on ttyACM0, CP2102N UART bridge on ttyUSB0, a reSpeaker XVF3800 4-mic USB array, an unidentified QDtech MPI5001 HID device, and Bluetooth radio). Networking shows a wired Ethernet default route up, Wi-Fi and CAN interfaces down, and two USB-gadget network interfaces up without IP addresses. No actuator inventory or camera devices were enumerated. All observed conditions are informational/advisory; no hardware fault has been directly verified from this passive snapshot.
highest_priority_next_check: Whether any ROS node is currently bound to /dev/ttyACM0 (STM32/mbed) or /dev/ttyUSB0 (CP2102N) — no publisher/subscriber or parameter-service linkage to these serial ports was captured.
successful_checks: CPU snapshot is below the warning threshold (0.0%).
Memory snapshot is below the warning threshold (60.2%).
No collected filesystem is at or above 90% usage.
ROS 2 graph discovery succeeded (0 nodes, 7 topics).
Default network route is present on enP8p1s0.
architecture_observations: Robot identity 'cutie' runs ROS 2 Humble with ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0 and default RMW; the graph was recovered from an already-running process rather than the operator's shell environment.

Topic names (/cutie/brain/status, /cutie/speaker/say, /cutie/speaker/status, /cutie/speech/text, /cutie/response/text) plus parameter services under /cutie_llm and /cutie_speaker indicate at least an LLM/brain node and a speaker node are intended to exist in the graph, even though 'nodes':0 was reported.

The reSpeaker XVF3800 4-mic USB array is the most likely physical backing for /cutie/speech/text (input) and /cutie/speaker/* (output) topics, based on naming correlation only — no direct ROS-to-device binding was captured.

An STMicroelectronics STM32 STLink board (ttyACM0, mbed drive, tiny 1.6MB block device 'sda') is present and read/write accessible to plugdev group; this is a common motor-controller/firmware-programming interface but no ROS driver reference confirms its role.

A Silicon Labs CP2102N USB-UART bridge (ttyUSB0) is present but not accessible to the current user (dialout group only); its consumer (if any) is not identified in the ROS graph or elsewhere in the snapshot.

A CAN interface (can0, mttcan driver) exists but is administratively down and MTU 16 (classic CAN framing), with no referencing ROS node or service — plausible drivetrain/actuator bus that is either unused or not yet brought up.

Two USB-gadget network interfaces (usb0, usb1) are up but carry no IPv4 address, and l4tbr0 (bridge) is down — suggests a host-tethering or inter-board USB network path that may be partially configured.
Wi-Fi (rtl88x2ce) is down while wired Ethernet (r8168, enP8p1s0) is the active default route — consistent with a docked/lab configuration rather than a fault.

The QDtech MPI5001 HID device (vendor 0484:5750) has no corresponding entry in sensor/actuator inventories or ROS topics; its function is unknown from this snapshot (name suggests a possible display/touch controller).
Storage, thermal, memory, and CPU metrics are all within normal operating bounds for this platform; swap usage (43.6%) is elevated but not yet at a level indicating pressure.
unknowns: Whether any ROS node is currently bound to /dev/ttyACM0 (STM32/mbed) or /dev/ttyUSB0 (CP2102N) — no publisher/subscriber or parameter-service linkage to these serial ports was captured.
The physical/functional purpose of the QDtech MPI5001 HID device and whether it is required by the robot profile.

Why the ROS graph reports 12 services under /cutie_llm and /cutie_speaker parameter-service namespaces yet 0 discovered nodes and 0 'detailed_nodes' — could be a discovery/daemon caching artifact or an environment/domain mismatch between the snapshot tool and the running graph.
Whether the CAN bus (can0) and USB-gadget network interfaces (usb0/usb1) are required for this robot's normal operation or are simply unused/reserved paths.
Whether the reSpeaker XVF3800 is actually the audio backend for the /cutie/speech and /cutie/speaker topics, or if that mapping is coincidental naming.

issues.title: Current user/process lacks read-write access to /dev/ttyUSB0 (CP2102N USB-UART)
issues.expected_state: Only serial interfaces required by the active robot profile or ROS runtime need stable read-write access; unused ports may legitimately remain access-restricted.
issues.operational_impact: No operational impact is proven; impact depends entirely on whether any running process (e.g., a microcontroller/actuator driver) needs this port, which is not confirmed in this snapshot.
observed: permissions=crw-rw----, owner=root:dialout, access=denied for /dev/ttyUSB0 and related /dev/char/188:0 node
No ROS topic, service, or node reference to ttyUSB0 or the CP2102N device was found in the snapshot
probable_causes: The invoking user/process is not a member of the 'dialout' group.
The port is intentionally unused at this time (no consumer configured).
A udev rule granting broader access (e.g., plugdev) was not applied for this specific device.
primary_approach: Confirm whether any ROS node, service, or startup script is expected to use /dev/ttyUSB0 before considering any permission change.
Inspect device ownership and any process currently holding or attempting to open the port via read-only probes.
alternative_approaches: Check udev rules and group memberships for the operator account via device_metadata/port_owner probes to understand why this port differs in permission model from ttyACM0 (which is plugdev, read-write).
success_criteria: It is confirmed whether /dev/ttyUSB0 is required by any active or intended robot function.
If required, the responsible process can open the port without permission denial (verified via port_owner/service_status, not by executing repairs).

issues.title: ROS installed but current shell/session not sourced; graph recovered indirectly
issues.expected_state: The configured ROS environment (ROS_DISTRO, ROS_DOMAIN_ID, RMW_IMPLEMENTATION) should be consistently sourced for the operator's session to guarantee deterministic discovery.
issues.operational_impact: Discovery performed by recovering environment variables from an already-running process; this is functional but means any operator-run ROS CLI commands in an unsourced shell may not see the same graph.
observed: Live graph was recovered using ROS_DISTRO=humble, ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0, RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=default from a running process
probable_causes: No .bashrc/.profile sourcing of the ROS underlay in the operator's shell.
Deliberate container/service-managed ROS runtime separate from the operator's interactive shell.
primary_approach: Before running any interactive ROS diagnostic commands, source the same ROS underlay/workspace and domain settings recovered by the runtime (ROS_DISTRO=humble, ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0) to ensure consistent discovery.
alternative_approaches: Use ros_param_list and ros_node_info probes against the already-running process's environment rather than relying on a freshly sourced shell, to avoid introducing a second, potentially mismatched discovery domain.
success_criteria: Ros2 CLI commands run in an operator shell return the same topic/service/node counts as the recovered runtime graph.
